summary: The host refuses automated reads: robots.txt and the sign-in page both answer HTTP 403 with a security check instead of their content, and no other public source shows the sign-in form.

sources.title: The catalog sign-in address, rendered once without an account: a challenge page, not the sign-in form
sources.note: Made before the capture standard was settled. Under that standard it would not have been made, because robots.txt on this host is refused. It is kept as a record of the refusal, supports no selector and does not raise the class.

staysInteractive.note: A challenge page with a Cloudflare Turnstile widget stood in front of the sign-in page in the capture. Whether an ordinary visible browser is challenged too was not determined.

lookedFor: robots.txt of www.networksolutions.com, read on the review date with a plain HTTP client: HTTP 403 and a page titled Security check | Network Solutions, which asks to complete the security check and says it protects the website from automated traffic. A refused robots.txt means the check did not come back clean.
The legal page on the same host: the same HTTP 403 security check, to a plain HTTP client and to a second automated reader. The help pages on that host were not attempted.

The Master Services Agreement (last updated January 22, 2026) and the Acceptable Use Policy (updated March 4, 2026) on legal.newfold.com: readable; neither restricts automated access to the website and neither describes the sign-in page.

The catalog address had already been rendered once, anonymously, in headless Edge (capture.json): HTTP 403 on the catalog host itself, with no hand-off to another host. It shows a challenge card with a Cloudflare Turnstile frame from challenges.cloudflare.com and one hidden response field; no form, no username field and no credential field. Nothing was typed or clicked and the page was not loaded again.
A code search on GitHub for the sign-in address: DNS setup guides and this repository's own catalog; nothing that reproduces the form.
neededFromUser: The sign-in page saved from the user's own browser as "Webpage, Complete" and read with the capture tool's --from-file mode, plus the page that follows the first step if the sign-in has two. That would make this class A. Save any page signed out and with no password typed in; keep the "_files" folder beside the .html and both outside the repository: they can hold the account name.
notes: The capture was requested on www.networksolutions.com and ended on the same host and path. Whether the capture file stays in the corpus is the lead's decision; if it is removed, the source entry here and the one in register-com go with it.
